exposure: maternal age: ≤15 years (early adolescent), 16-19 years (late adolescent), and 20-30 years (adult)
finding: Early adolescent pregnancy (≤15 years) was associated with higher risks of preterm birth, growth restriction, and low birthweight compared to late adolescence (16-19 years) and adult pregnancies (20-30 years), but cesarean section rates were lower in the early adolescent group.
mod_finding: Cesarean rate was significantly lower in early adolescent mothers.
